=== BEGIN PROMPT A902_S18B_LakeForestPlus_Cam_04_v1 ===

Create one photorealistic interior concept of apartment A-902, S18B Lake Forest Plus, Cam_04. The objective is direct fidelity to the supplied original Lake Forest villa materials and furniture character.

INPUT ORDER. Image 1: 04_renderek/semleges_v2b/A902_semlegesv2b_3_master.png. Subsequent images: references/LF12.jpg, references/LF13.jpg, references/LF15.jpg. Keep this input order. If a named camera control is unresolved, assemble it before generation; never substitute a different camera.

SITE EVIDENCE INPUTS. Also attach 08_allapotfelmeres/fotok_profi_20261025/A902/KZS_3741-491.jpg, 08_allapotfelmeres/fotok_profi_20261025/A902/KZS_3771-461.jpg, 08_allapotfelmeres/fotok_profi_20261025/A902/KZS_3753-479.jpg. These photographs are authority for existing floor, tile, window finish and panorama only; they do not replace Image 1 or redefine its camera.

ORIGINAL LAKE FOREST IDENTITY. Reproduce the supplied original April 20, 2024 Lake Forest villa B-design, not a loose interpretation of luxury. Match the actual reference surfaces: strongly grained grey-brown wood M01, warm brown/taupe stone appearance with fine pale veins M02, white mineral appearance with grey-gold veins M03, restrained brushed bronze/copper-brown metal M05, and off-white finely flecked woven upholstery M06. Material identifiers are visual reference IDs, not manufacturer codes. Keep their relative colour, grain scale, gloss and edges faithful to the reference photograph. Do not invent a stone brand or silently replace an original material with a cheaper imitation. Exact material composition and procurement remain unverified. This is a concept image, not proof of product identity. In S18B, the television backing is the broad bronze field from LF09; the kitchen has the pale grey clouded mineral surface, ivory tall doors and wood uppers of LF10; the master has the exact figurative mosaic panel of LF12. These B-specific assignments take precedence over the shared palette. Do not mix in the A brown TV backing or A all-stone headboard.

CAMERA. Use fixed Cam_04, looking northeast at the master bedroom from the southwest, 20 mm at 1.50 m. The east headboard and bed provide the central composition, with bedside surfaces readable and the complete north wardrobe wall visibly closing its existing niche. The south wardrobe strip belongs to the room and retains its actual visibility at the edge of the locked frame. Let layered evening light reveal upholstery and front divisions without enlarging the room.

APARTMENT LOCK. A-902 keeps the existing V3.3 camera identities and architectural shell, nominally 2.90 m in principal rooms, with actual lower local ceilings preserved. Keep the west W01 TV wall and the approved seating location facing it, using the original Lake Forest sofa detailing within the project's 3.00 x 2.40 m U-layout study; this is not a confirmed catalogue product or an approved change to the apartment shell. Do not inherit S07's Wolke L-sofa, pearl arcs or pale-oak table. Retain the established dining location, actual U-like/two-run kitchen and door/control clearances. The six base cameras remain Cam_12, Cam_02, Cam_03, Cam_04, Cam_11c and Cam_10; no professional photograph may be renamed as one of these. The original roof terrace levels, WPC steps, planted areas, rails and Budapest panorama remain unchanged.

ROOM DESIGN — ORIGINAL LAKE FOREST B MASTER IDENTITY. LF12 is the exact headboard reference: the large figurative mosaic-style composition with pale outlined human figures, taupe/grey tessellated areas and a warm reddish-brown patterned centre, framed by brown fine-veined sides. Preserve the original figures, composition, colour distribution and tessera-like texture; do not replace it with generic abstract art or a new painting. Its physical fabrication and original art/material asset must be resolved before procurement; this prompt does not claim a printed panel equals an original mosaic. Scale the whole artwork proportionally to the real headboard field, without cropping a figure merely to fill the wall. Continue LF13's satin taupe/bronze-brown closed cabinetry, softly rounded fixed ends and fine bronze pulls where the existing cabinet geometry allows. Any real vanity/desk uses LF13's light rounded furniture, oval bronze-rimmed mirror and white grey-gold veined fixed accent only if such a furniture footprint already exists. Do not add a dressing table where the model has none. Keep the low bed in its original apartment position, with white linen, finely speckled off-white pillows and woven throw, matching bedside pieces and a pale rug. Maintain approximately 3 m of concealed Hue headboard light, two Hue Go bedside lamps and independently controlled wardrobe interior light; do not invent the villa's pair of ceiling drops beside the bed. The wardrobe uses LF15's satin taupe base with bronze outlined diagonal dark and tinted-mirror inserts, each interrupted at its real door joint. Retain the actual window, curtains and floor.

ELECTRICAL POINTS. the master room’s existing ceiling point; inherited D20 headboard, D21/D23 bedside and D26 wardrobe feeds require room/point verification before use. These are plan-based identifiers and candidates, not an on-site electrical sign-off.

ARCHITECTURE AND CONTINUITY. Image 1, the named apartment control, governs the camera, crop, lens perspective, wall and ceiling outlines, openings and furniture placement. The villa images govern materials and furniture detailing only. Never borrow the villa room proportions, dark window frames, forest view, stairs, fireplace or ceiling coves. Retain the apartment's actual existing flooring from its site photograph, including plank direction, knots and tone; a neutral control's generic floor shader is not material evidence. Preserve actual wet-room tile, grey doors, white interior window frames, service lids, switches and heating/cooling ceiling fields. Unassigned walls and ceiling remain existing white; new finishes occur only on the specified furniture and mounted decorative fields. Keep the established furniture footprints and clearances; the expressly requested full-height headboard/panel surface may replace the shallow placeholder backing within the same wall plane and allowed build-up; scale reference detailing to fit those objects without moving an opening or shrinking the room contents. Full-height cabinetry closes to the actual local ceiling with a concealed installation allowance. Maintain the same material maps and object transforms in every view.

LIGHTING AND PHOTOGRAPHY. Render a realistic, carefully exposed architectural photograph with restrained 2700 K evening illumination and readable material texture; where a real window is visible retain its genuine daylight or blue-hour view. Dimmable Philips Hue-compatible warm-white ambience may operate between 2200 and 2700 K. Concealed strips must sit in aluminium profiles with opal diffusers and physical shielding; no visible LED dots or bright lines reflected in the screen or mirror. Use furniture-mounted light details and accessible ventilated drivers at the documented existing supply points only. No new ceiling cove, false ceiling, recessed spotlight, invented socket or drilling into a heating/cooling field. A decorative fixture is conditional on mounting, load and electrical compatibility at its original outlet. Technical and wet-zone approval remain pending. Preserve natural whites and the distinction between brown stone, grey-brown timber and bronze; avoid an orange wash that makes everything beige. Landscape output in the exact control aspect ratio, straight verticals, believable reflections, no people, no lettering, no watermark and no collage.

REJECT IF: the room grows, the camera moves, a window is invented, the WSG floor is recoloured, the original material hierarchy disappears, the sofa turns into a cloud-shaped generic product, the original figurative mosaic headboard is replaced by unrelated art or a pearl padded wall, or the TV field turns into a generic pale travertine wall. Render only physically visible elements; a reverse view must not pull hidden furniture around a corner. Do not use any earlier S07 furnished image as a material authority. This S18 concept requires subsequent geometry, original-material, electrical and full-budget validation.

=== END PROMPT A902_S18B_LakeForestPlus_Cam_04_v1 ===

ACTUAL INPUT ORDER OVERRIDES PREVIOUS INPUT PARAGRAPH: image 1 is the exact furnished Cam_04 bedroom in the owner's 17-style selector and is the EDIT TARGET for exact camera, room proportions, bed position, existing floor, wardrobe outer dimensions, ceiling, doors and pathways. Subsequent images are original Lake Forest villa reference materials and details ONLY. Replace old pearl arcs, fabric headboard and pale old-style cabinetry completely with the original Lake Forest B material hierarchy. Use LF12 original floor-to-ceiling figurative mosaic HEADBOARD with outlined pale human figures and warm reddish-brown patterned field, exactly the reference composition scaled into existing headboard, not invented modern art. Brown finely veined flanks. Use LF15 satin taupe full-height wardrobe fronts with diagonal bronze framed tinted mirror insets, matching original; no grained wood base. Fully furnished master suite: crisp white linen bedding and pale textured throw, finely woven cushions, pale rug, matching bedside cabinets with two warm Hue Go lights, concealed ~3m headboard light diffused behind panel, wardrobe lighting only where physically visible. Full-height curtain layers on real windows if in frame, never invent an opening. Retain adequate space to open wardrobe doors. Mirror insets reflect this exact bedroom plausibly. No villa skylight, ceiling recess or new spotlights. No pendant obstructing this view; preserve existing ceiling. Bright readable neutral fill with controlled warm layered light, no orange wash or dark hotel rendering. Single landscape image, no text.
